items.t: Diwali 2026 bank holidays: How many days will banks be closed next week?
sum: Dhanteras marks the beginning of the 5-days of Diwali. Meanwhile in banks, customers are advised to check their local holiday calendar before heading to their bank branch in Diwali days

Even though the week is busy with Diwali festivities, banks also have a heavy work schedule. Customers are reminded to check their local holiday calendar before visiting their bank branch, even though there isn't a national holiday this week.

Customers can easily continue their financial transactions via internet banking, ATMs, and UPI during a holiday, but branch-based operations including cash deposits and check-related work would be suspended during holidays.

The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) holiday calendar lists regional bank closures for Diwali, Govardhan Puja, Laxmi Puja and Bhai Dooj across different parts of the country. However, these holidays are not uniform nationwide and vary by location.

Banks will also stay open tomorrow on Saturday, November 7, as it is the first Saturday of the month, despite Choti Diwali festivity. Customers can anticipate regular access to in-branch banking facilities, subject to individual branch timings.
November 7: Despite Choti Diwali falling on Saturday, it will be a regular working day nationwide.
November 8: Weekly Sunday holiday with main Diwali Laxmi Pujan.

SBI Card stock in focus after profit rises on lower credit costs
sum: SBI Cards and Payment Services reported a sharp rise in second-quarter profit on October 23, 2026, as improving asset quality reduced provisions. Reuters, published by The Hindu BusinessLine, reported that profit after tax reached INR 778 crore for the quarter ended September 30, compared with INR 445 crore a year earlier.

Loan-loss provisions fell 36.6 percent year over year to INR 819 crore. Gross non-performing assets stood at 1.90 percent at the end of September, down 14 basis points from three months earlier, after the company tightened credit underwriting to address delinquencies.

Total revenue from operations rose 3.6 percent year over year to INR 5,141 crore. Card spending increased 3 percent to INR 1.11 lakh crore, while cards-in-force grew 8 percent to 23.2 million. The figures point to continued volume growth, although the earnings improvement was driven more clearly by lower credit costs than by revenue expansion.

SBI Card's next focus is balancing expansion in card usage with underwriting discipline. Retail and corporate spending supported credit growth in the September quarter, while the lower provision burden gives profitability more room if asset quality remains stable.

SBI Cards and Payment Services issues credit cards in India and serves consumer and corporate spending needs. The company is a unit of State Bank of India and operates in the Indian payments and consumer-finance market. Its business combines card issuance, transaction spending and credit underwriting, making asset quality and funding costs central investment considerations.

Why SBI shares fell sharply after Q2
sum: State Bank of India faced a sharp stock pullback as soaring bond yields and rising operating expenses dragged core operating profits well below expectations, despite headline earnings getting a lift from one-off subsidiary stake sales. Discover how analysts view the true underlying valuation of its vast subsidiary network.

State Bank of India beat street estimates with both the topline and net profit. The net interest margin beat expectations, driven by strong credit growth and continued asset-quality improvement. Yet the stock fell sharply by 4.5% from the day's high to the day's low of ₹961.2, soon after the second-quarter earnings were released, before recovering slightly.
That's because the operating profit was well below estimates.

The country's largest bank booked a ₹7,288 crore pre-tax gain from selling a 6.3% stake in SBI Funds Management. The company also made ₹2,410 crore, net of taxes, from selling shares in the recently concluded National Stock Exchange (NSE) IPO. However, the profit has been credited to capital reserves, not the profit and loss statement.

We were expecting around ₹17,000 crore in other income during this quarter, but it has come at around ₹11,000 crore. So maybe certain treasury loss has come into the picture due to hardening of yields. SAMEER SAWANT, RESEARCH ANALYST, MIRAE ASSET SHAREKHAN

Regulations require all Indian banks to hold a portion of their reserves in government bonds. Compared money in government securities, making them vulnerable to sharp swings in yields. The recent increase in government bond yields requires them to mark down the value of their investments.

The sharp deviation between profit after tax and operating profit suggests underlying weakness. Cost pressures are visible. Operating expenses rose 9.6% year on year and 15.6% in the last three months. Cost-to-income ratio worsened to 49.82% by September 2026 from 46.71% at the end of June 2026.

Sensex jumps 765 points during early trade on sharp rally in Reliance shares, decline in oil prices
sum: Stock market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty surged in early trade on Monday, driven by a sharp rally in bellwether Reliance Industries post earnings announcement and cooling crude oil prices.
Foreign fund inflows and a positive trend in Asian equities also added to the markets optimism during the initial trading.
The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 764.72 points to 75,216.80 in early trade. The 50-share NSE Nifty surged 201.40 points to 23,255.90.

From the 30 Sensex firms, Reliance Industries jumped over 6 per cent after the firm posted a record quarterly profit of Rs 29,550 crore for July-September, up 33.8 per cent from a year earlier, as its oil-to-chemicals business rode a surge in global fuel margins and growth in its telecom arm offset the relatively subdued performance in retail.
NTPC, Tata Steel, Power Grid, Maruti and State Bank of India were also among the gainers.
Sun Pharma, Tech Mahindra, Titan and Infosys were trading lower.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded 3 per cent lower at USD 110 per barrel.

Stock markets to track geopolitical developments, oil prices, earnings this week: Analysts
sum: New Delhi: Geopolitical developments, especially growing concerns about renewed conflict between the US and Iran, crude oil prices, and quarterly earnings will be the major drivers for stock markets this week, analysts said.
In addition, US midterm elections, foreign investor trading activity, and macroeconomic data announcements will also be tracked by market investors.

“Markets will remain focused on the September quarter earnings season, key economic data releases and global developments this week. Investors will assess corporate performance for signs of sustained revenue growth, margin resilience and improving demand. Banking results will offer insights into credit growth, deposit mobilisation and asset quality, while automobile, consumer and industrial companies will provide a broader assessment of domestic demand conditions,” Ajit Mishra, SVP â€“ Research, Religare Broking, said.
Crude oil prices will remain an important variable, with elevated levels amid geopolitical uncertainty posing risks to imported inflation, the rupee and corporate margins, he said.
Movements in US Treasury yields, foreign institutional investor flows and currency markets will also influence near-term sentiment and the sustainability of the recent recovery, Mishra added.

“Key events to watch this week include the US midterm elections, US PMI and India’s HSBC PMI. On the earnings front, M&M, Bajaj Finserv, ITC, Dabur, Apollo Hospitals, BSE, Cummins India and Hindalco will be in focus,” Siddhartha Khemka – Head of Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said.
Among other companies scheduled to announce their earnings this week are Lupin, NSE, State Bank of India, Apollo Tyres, LIC, ONGC and Titan.
